title: Adopt ctl-meta current-read and resource-safety provider without downstream fork
purpose: Record downstream adoption of ctl-meta current-read and resource-safety dogfood tooling as the canonical reader for CTL current-state and resource-safety queries, while keeping twisted-yetter's local ctl_store.py as a thin adapter rather than a fork.
claim_boundary: This note records tooling and provider-policy adoption only. It does not assert a new twisted-yetter mathematical result, does not change ctl-kernel/1 semantics, and does not import ctl-meta's project-local normative CTL state.

adoption_boundary.adoption_type: downstream provider adoption of CTL current-read tooling

downstream_adapter.policy: Delegate to ctl-meta/meta/ctl-dogfood/scripts/ctl_store.py, normalize repo-local absolute --path arguments to repo-relative paths, and inject --store-root for the twisted-yetter ctl-dogfood store when the caller did not provide one.
non_fork_checks: adapter preserves path_hygiene_report as a subprocess-backed compatibility API for existing downstream tests
adapter path normalization is CLI ergonomics only and does not reimplement CTL current-read or resource-safety logic

current_read_discipline.discipline_summary: Current-state and resource-safety answers must be grounded in replayed CTL current root, active bindings, and ResourceSafetyStatus overlays. Filesystem search is acceptable for discovery or archaeology, not as the final current-state source.
current_read_discipline.resource_safety_registration_policy: Reusable evaluators, scripts, generated artifacts, and lab notes that become known-wrong, deprecated, superseded, or replacement-critical should be registered as ctl-resource handle/snapshot/safety-status claims rather than relying only on file headers or prose notes.

repo_snapshot.dirty_status_summary: No unrelated dirty files were present before this resource-safety adoption update. This update edits the provider-adoption preimage, the thin ctl_store.py adapter, current-read tests, and new ctl-dogfood/resources payloads before admission; admission then writes CTL objects, manifests, and refs/main.json.

source_of_truth_policy: This is a machine-readable CTL lab-note preimage. The admitted claim for this payload is the current provider-adoption record.
